title: Circular group nesting
suggestedFix: Break the loop in Active Directory Users and Computers: remove one nested member so the chain is a tree. Circular nesting makes effective membership unpredictable and can loop token evaluation.

title: Nesting depth 4 (limit 3)
detail: Depth-5 sits 4 groups above its deepest nested member chain.
suggestedFix: Flatten the chain. Nesting more than three groups deep is hard to audit and often leftover from old role groups. Prefer one role group and direct members.

title: Empty security group
detail: Enterprise Admins is a security group with no members.
suggestedFix: If unused, document and delete it after checking delegated ACLs and file shares. Empty groups linger and get reused by mistake.

title: Disabled user still in groups
detail: Bob Martinez is disabled but remains in Finance-App.
suggestedFix: Remove the disabled account from application and role groups (leave Domain Users). Disabled members still appear in nested token expansion and confuse access reviews.

title: Stale user still in groups
detail: Carol Singh has no logon in 90+ days (or never) and is still in Finance, All-Staff.
suggestedFix: Confirm the account is unused, then disable it and strip role-group membership. Stale members are a common source of leftover access in small directories.

title: Redundant direct membership
detail: Alice Chen is a direct member of IT-Admins and of nested group Helpdesk.
suggestedFix: Remove the user from the parent (IT-Admins) or from the nested group — not both. Keep the membership that matches the actual role.

title: Redundant direct membership

title: Nested path to Domain Admins
detail: Alice Chen → IT-Admins → Tier0 → Domain Admins | Alice Chen → Helpdesk → IT-Admins → Tier0 → Domain Admins
suggestedFix: Review why Alice Chen reaches Domain Admins through nested groups. Privileged groups should have direct, named members only.

title: Distribution group nested in a security group
detail: All-Staff (distribution) is a member of Corp-Security (security).
suggestedFix: Do not nest distribution groups into security groups. Mail-enabled dist groups are not meant to grant access. Create a security group for the role and keep the dist group for email only.
